entities.label: Idea
entities.summary:
**Paragraph 1 — Identity & Significance**: Windows 95 was a groundbreaking personal computer operating system developed by Microsoft, specifically designed for the mass market, and released in 1995 CE. It was the first widely adopted operating system to integrate a graphical user interface (GUI), making it accessible to a broad audience, particularly in the Global North. The creation of Windows 95 marked a significant shift in the computing landscape, as it catered to the needs of a new generation of users who demanded user-friendly interfaces and increased productivity.


**Paragraph 2 — What Happened**: The development of Windows 95 involved significant advancements in hardware and software, including the introduction of 32-bit processors, improved graphics capabilities, and a user-friendly interface that featured the now-iconic Start menu. This operating system was instrumental in popularizing the concept of a 'home computer' and transforming the way people worked, communicated, and entertained themselves. The widespread adoption of Windows 95 also spurred the growth of the technology industry, creating new job opportunities and driving innovation in related fields.


**Paragraph 3 — Legacy & Consequence**: The impact of Windows 95 can still be seen in modern operating systems, such as its modern successors, Windows 10 and Windows 11. The influence of Windows 95 also extends to the broader technology sector, with many companies adopting similar GUI designs and user interfaces. Furthermore, the legacy of Windows 95 can be observed in the way technology is integrated into everyday life, from mobile devices to the Internet of Things (IoT).


**Closing Statistic**: With over 1 billion copies sold worldwide, Windows 95 remains one of the best-selling operating systems of all time, a testament to its enduring impact on the technology industry.
